official.deadline_note: MOE publishes no single deadline date. Each authorized ROC overseas office sets the deadline in the scholarship guidelines it issues for its own jurisdiction (offices are required to issue their guidelines by January 31 each year); applications are usually due in January or February.
official.application_cycle: Annual round; overseas offices issue their own guidelines by 31 January each year and receive applications usually in January or February
official.status_note: The MOE Huayu Enrichment Scholarship page is live and unchanged in substance; the current Operation Directions were amended on 4 February 2025. As of the verification date the most recent application round (usually January-February) has passed, so the next round is expected in January-February 2027 for courses beginning in the following academic year (scholarship period 1 September - 31 August, summer courses excepted).
official.tuition_coverage_note: MOE's official scholarship comparison table lists 'Tuition and Miscellaneous Expenses: N/A' for the Huayu Enrichment Scholarship; the monthly stipend is the only published financial support.
benefits: Monthly stipend of NT$28,000 (NTD 28,000 each month), disbursed monthly from the month the recipient begins studies until the scholarship period ends.
Stipend duration matched to the awarded course: a 2-month summer course, or a 3-month, 6-month, 9-month or one-year course.
Recipients enrol at an MOE-approved Chinese language center affiliated with a university or college that can enrol students overseas.
eligibility: Foreign persons at least 18 years old who have graduated from secondary school or have studied at post-secondary level, have an excellent academic record, and are of good moral character.
Not eligible: overseas compatriot students and ROC (Taiwan) passport holders; the Directions' purpose clause also excludes people from mainland China, Hong Kong or Macao.
Not eligible: a person currently studying Chinese in Taiwan or who has previously undertaken a degree programme in Taiwan.
Not eligible: a person who has previously received a Huayu Enrichment Scholarship, a TUSA Global Ambassador Scholarship, or a Taiwan Scholarship.
Not eligible: exchange students in Taiwan under an academic cooperation agreement, and persons studying or researching in Taiwan while receiving other Taiwan government or institutional funding.

Exception: the graduation and academic-record exclusions do not apply to a foreign national recommended or selected by a foreign government, institution or educational institution under an education cooperation agreement.
requirements: Apply to the authorized overseas office in your country of nationality (or the office with jurisdiction over Taiwan-related matters) before the deadline in that office's own guidelines.
Submit all five required document types, including proof of having already applied to a Chinese language center.
Choose an MOE-approved Chinese language center affiliated with a university or college and apply to it separately, on its own timeline.
Recipients must undertake at least 15 hours of required language classes each week and complete enrolment within the set period.
One-year recipients who complete at least one term may transfer once to another approved center; shorter awards cannot transfer.
documents: Photocopy of the applicant's passport, or other documentation that is adequate proof of nationality
Photocopy of proof of the applicant's highest education level and photocopies of related transcripts
Photocopy of documentary proof that the applicant has already applied to a Chinese language center (for example, a photocopy of the application-for-admission form)
Any other document(s) required by the authorized overseas office
selection_criteria: Selection is made by each authorized overseas office through document review or personal interview, with the procedure set out in that office's own guidelines.

Offices allocate and reallocate quotas; if a selected candidate waives the offer before arriving in Taiwan the office may give the place to another suitable candidate (no reallocation after March 31 of the following year).
coverage: Monthly stipend of NT$28,000 for the awarded course period.
No tuition or miscellaneous-fee support: MOE's comparison table records 'Tuition and Miscellaneous Expenses: N/A' for HES.
No airfare, accommodation or insurance support is published for HES (one-way plane tickets are a feature of the separate MOFA Taiwan Scholarship).
application_method: Submit the required documents to the authorized ROC overseas office for your country of nationality, or the authorized office with jurisdiction over Taiwan-related matters there, before that office's published deadline.
Apply separately for admission to your chosen MOE-approved Chinese language center and submit proof of that application with the scholarship package.
After selection, the overseas office confirms eligibility once you send a photocopy of the language center's admission notice (due by June 30).
official.application_route: Paper/document application to the ROC (Taiwan) overseas mission covering your country of nationality before its own January-February deadline, plus a separate admission application to a university-affiliated Chinese language center
official.citizenship_residency: Foreign nationals only; ROC (Taiwan) passport holders and overseas compatriot students are excluded, and the Directions' purpose clause excludes people from mainland China, Hong Kong and Macao
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the scholarship exists for foreign nationals, who apply through the ROC overseas office covering their country of nationality
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Study must be at an MOE-approved Chinese language center affiliated with a university or college in Taiwan that can enrol students overseas
official.duration: A 2-month summer course (June-July or July-August), or a 3-month, 6-month, 9-month or one-year course; for non-summer awards the scholarship period runs 1 September to 31 August of the following year and cannot be deferred or interrupted
official.description: Taiwan's Ministry of Education established the Huayu Enrichment Scholarship to encourage international students to study Huayu (Mandarin Chinese) in the Republic of China (Taiwan) and become aware of Taiwanese culture and society. It provides a monthly stipend of NT$28,000 for a 2-month summer course or a 3-month, 6-month, 9-month or one-year course at an approved university-affiliated Chinese language center.
official.program_type: Government non-degree Mandarin Chinese language scholarship (Ministry of Education Huayu Enrichment Scholarship, awarded through ROC overseas missions)

not_confirmed: deadline_date (MOE publishes no single date; each overseas office sets its own)
travel_coverage (no travel support published for HES)
english_requirement (no English test requirement published; the course is Mandarin study)
verification.notes: The NT$28,000 monthly stipend and the full eligibility, application and conduct rules were verified on MOE's live HES page and the current Operation Directions Governing the MOE Huayu Enrichment Scholarships (amended 4 February 2025); the previously stored URL pointed at the different Taiwan Scholarship page, which does not govern HES.

applicant_utility.summary: HES is a stipend-only award: NT$28,000 a month for a 2-month summer or 3-, 6-, 9- or 12-month Mandarin course, with tuition, flights and accommodation left to you. You must apply twice - once to the ROC overseas office covering your nationality and once separately to a university-affiliated Chinese language centre - and only the overseas office's own January-February deadline matters. Anyone who has previously held an HES, Taiwan Scholarship or TUSA Global Ambassador Scholarship is permanently barred, so audit your history before investing effort.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Adults 18 or over seeking a funded Mandarin immersion in Taiwan who can hit an overseas office's January-February deadline; the 6-month and longer options suit learners who also want part-time work rights.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you clear all five exclusions (ROC passport or overseas compatriot status, currently studying Chinese in Taiwan, a previous degree in Taiwan, a prior HES/TUSA/Taiwan Scholarship, exchange or existing Taiwan funding).
Identify your ROC overseas office and check its HES guidelines as soon as they are issued (offices must publish them by 31 January).
Apply to your chosen MOE-approved university-affiliated Chinese language centre early, because proof of that application is a mandatory scholarship document.
Prepare the passport copy, highest-education proof with transcripts, and the HES application form before the window opens.
If you target a 9-month or longer award, check whether you already hold a TOCFL Band B Level 3 certificate from the past two years; if not, plan to sit the test in Taiwan at your own expense.
common_rejection_risks: Missing the overseas office's own deadline - MOE sets none centrally and each office runs its own calendar.
Failing to supply documentary proof that you already applied to a Chinese language centre.
A previous HES, Taiwan Scholarship or TUSA Global Ambassador Scholarship award, which is an outright bar even if unused.
Incomplete highest-education proof or transcripts, or extra documents demanded by the specific overseas office.
Leaving the language centre admission notice photocopy unsent to the overseas office past 30 June, which forfeits the award.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Language-centre tuition and miscellaneous fees (HES pays none), return airfare, housing, daily living costs, National Health Insurance premiums once you have been in Taiwan six months (which the language centre may deduct from your monthly stipend), and TOCFL test fees.
document_audit: The proof-of-application document must show you applied to the language centre before the scholarship deadline; an acceptance letter is not required, but the application record is.
Your passport copy must match the nationality under which you apply, because offices only handle their own jurisdictions.
Transcripts must evidence your highest education level; the office may require further documents under its own guidelines.
alerts: The award is not deferrable: non-summer courses must run 1 September to 31 August, the period cannot be interrupted, and failure to use it in that window is treated as losing eligibility.
Missing 12 or more hours of required classes in a single month suspends the stipend for a month, an average below 80 triggers suspension, and two consecutive terms below 80 revoke the award.
Only recipients on courses of six months or longer may work; shorter awards are study-only.
Concurrent receipt of any other Taiwan government or institutional funding cancels eligibility and forces repayment of the overlapping months.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Post or deliver the five-document package to your ROC overseas office by its January-February deadline; the office screens documents or interviews, confirms your language-centre admission by June, and issues the scholarship certificate before you travel.

official.deadline_note: TIGP publishes a recurring annual window rather than one fixed calendar date: applications are received online from November to February each year (GMT+8). The exact closing date for the next cycle is fixed in the application announcement TIGP posts each November, so confirm it there before relying on a date.
official.application_cycle: Annual November-February application round for entry in the following fall semester
official.status_note: The November-February window for the most recent cycle has closed (it ran November 2025 to February 2026); the next round is expected to open in November 2026. Admitted students are enrolled in the subsequent fall semester.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Tuition is not waived. Academia Sinica subsidises the difference between the higher international and lower domestic tuition fees for five consecutive years, during which international students pay the same as domestic students - generally around NT$28,000-31,000 per semester for the first four semesters and around NT$16,000-20,000 per semester for the remainder, varying by partner university.
benefits: Tax-free stipend of NT$40,000 per month (NT$34,000 + NT$6,000) for the first year.
For students who perform well, the scholarship/stipend is extended for one more year.
Academia Sinica subsidises the international/domestic tuition-fee difference for five consecutive years, so international students pay the domestic tuition rate.
Access to separate competitive awards on top of the stipend: Presidential Fellowship, Research Performance Fellowship, Rising Star Fellowship, PhD Supplemental Stipend Program and Travel Grants.
eligibility: Applicants must hold a bachelor's and/or master's degree in science, arts, or related disciplines; final-year students may apply by selecting the 'will be obtained' option for their degree.
An English proficiency test score (TOEFL, IELTS, GEPT or TOEIC) is required, except for applicants to the EAMW programme, who submit other language proficiency test scores instead.
Applicants may apply to ONE TIGP programme only.
There is no set research-experience requirement, though demonstrated research experience can strengthen an application.
requirements: Apply online through TIGP's application portal during the November-February window and meet the general requirements plus the chosen programme's own requirements.
An academic transcript for coursework completed post high school, three letters of reference, and a statement of purpose are required; GRE general and subject tests are optional.
English test scores must have been taken within the past two years.
Select a thesis advisor before the end of the first year of study.
Uphold the academic integrity standards of Academia Sinica and the partner university.
documents: Online application in TIGP's portal with electronic files, including the academic records for the qualification stated.
Three letters of reference, submitted online by referees through TIGP's recommendation portal.
English proficiency test score report (TOEFL, IELTS, GEPT or TOEIC; other language scores for the EAMW programme).
If you pass the preliminary evaluation: original academic transcripts (preferably registrar-sealed) and original language test reports, sent by post to the TIGP Office.
selection_criteria: Admission is decided separately by each Ph.D. programme; applications are evaluated by a group of professors/research fellows and one-on-one advisorship is usually not compulsory for most programmes.
Programmes may differ in standardized-test requirements (English proficiency, GRE subject scores) and other detailed criteria, so each programme's own admission criteria apply.
There is no set research-experience requirement; publications or other supporting documentation can strengthen the profile.
coverage: Tax-free stipend of NT$40,000 per month (NT$34,000 + NT$6,000) for the first year, extendable by one further year for students who perform well.
The international/domestic tuition differential is subsidised for five consecutive years, leaving students paying the domestic rate themselves.
No airfare, accommodation or insurance support is stated in the core scholarship/stipend description; Travel Grants are a separate competitive award.
After the scholarship/stipend allowance period, further financial support depends on the individual thesis advisor.
application_method: Create an account, compile the application materials and submit through TIGP's online application portal (http://tigp.apps.sinica.edu.tw/index.php) between November and February each year.
Enter your referees' information in the portal so they can access the online recommendation portal.
If you pass the preliminary evaluation, post original academic transcripts and original English test reports (institution CODE 7142, NAME Academia Sinica) to the TIGP Office before the deadline.
official.application_route: Single online application via TIGP's portal (tigp.apps.sinica.edu.tw) during the November-February window; shortlisted candidates then post original transcripts and test reports to the TIGP Office in Taipei
official.international_eligibility: Yes - TIGP admits international applicants to its English-taught Ph.D. programmes; the published general requirements are written for international applicants
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Applicants choose one of TIGP's Ph.D. programmes and only one application is permitted per applicant
official.research_requirement: No set research-experience requirement; a statement of purpose is required, programme-level research proposals or interviews may apply, and a thesis advisor must be selected before the end of the first year
official.duration: Ph.D. programme at a partner university; the stipend is paid for the first year and, for students who perform well, extended for one more year
official.description: The Taiwan International Graduate Program, run by Academia Sinica with partner universities, admits international students to English-taught Ph.D. programmes and provides a tax-free stipend of NT$40,000 per month for the first year, extendable for students who perform well, while Academia Sinica subsidises the international tuition differential for five consecutive years.
official.program_type: English-taught research Ph.D. scholarship/stipend programme administered by Academia Sinica with partner universities
official.english_requirement: TOEFL iBT 79-80 (TOEFL-ITP not accepted), IELTS Academic overall Band Score of at least 5.5, GEPT High-Intermediate level, or TOEIC Listening and Reading score of at least 785; scores must be from the past two years. Waivers are accepted for nationals of listed English-speaking countries, applicants with two or more years of full-time study in English, or a highest degree entirely taught in English (medium-of-instruction certificate), subject to each programme's discretion. Applicants to the EAMW programme submit other language proficiency test scores.

not_confirmed: exact calendar deadline for the next cycle (TIGP publishes only the November-February window; confirm in the November announcement)
travel_coverage (no airfare or travel support in the core stipend; Travel Grants are separate competitive awards)
verification.notes: The NT$40,000/month (NT$34,000 + NT$6,000) stipend, the five-year tuition-differential subsidy, domestic tuition ranges, living-cost budget, English test thresholds and the November-February window were all read directly on TIGP's official pages; an older FAQ entry citing NT$34,000 is superseded by the current stipend page.

applicant_utility.summary: Admission to a TIGP Ph.D. programme carries a tax-free NT$40,000 monthly stipend for the first year, extended one more year for strong performers, plus a subsidy that caps your fees at the domestic rate for five years - but tuition itself is never waived. You apply online once a year between November and February, there is no application fee, and you may apply to only one programme. After the stipend period, funding depends on your thesis advisor, so choosing an advisor is a financial decision as much as an academic one.
applicant_utility.best_fit: International bachelor's or master's graduates in science, arts or related disciplines seeking a fully English-taught, funded research PhD in Taiwan who can self-fund domestic-rate tuition from month one.
application_readiness_checklist: Pick exactly one TIGP programme and read that programme's own admissions page - criteria, English requirements and interview practice differ by programme.
Book TOEFL or IELTS early: scores must be under two years old at application and TOEFL-ITP is not accepted.
Line up three referees and enter their details in the portal so their recommendations can be submitted online.
Shape the statement of purpose around the chosen programme's research strengths; GRE is optional but subject scores can strengthen the file.
If you plan to claim an English-medium-of-instruction waiver, obtain the MOI certificate or degree evidence from your registrar now.
common_rejection_risks: Applying to more than one programme - only one application is permitted.
Expired English test scores (older than two years) or a TOEFL-ITP score in place of iBT.
Programme-specific mismatches: wrong disciplinary background, missing subject GRE where a programme expects it, or an unprepared interview.
Budgeting as if NT$40,000 covers fees - it does not, and semester tuition of roughly NT$28,000-31,000 falls on you for the first four semesters.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Domestic-rate tuition (about NT$28,000-31,000 per semester for the first four semesters, NT$16,000-20,000 per semester thereafter), flights to Taiwan, and - on the programme's own Taipei figures - accommodation of about NT$5,000-14,000, food NT$6,000-10,000 and study/personal costs NT$1,000-3,000 per month; the stipend broadly covers the living items but leaves little margin.
document_audit: Shortlisted candidates must post original transcripts - preferably sealed from the registrar; notarized copies are accepted but self-notarization is not, and screenshots or plain photocopies are rejected.
Send English test reports under Academia Sinica's institution code 7142, or post the original report from the testing body.
Submitted materials are never returned, so send originals only when required and keep a full personal copy set.
alerts: The window is only November-February (GMT+8) and announcements appear late in the year, so monitor the site from October.
Final-year students should choose the 'will be obtained' option and email the scanned diploma to the programme secretary the moment it is conferred.
Funding beyond the stipend period is advisor-dependent, and advisor selection is due before the end of the first year - secure a funded supervisor early.
Academic-integrity breaches can cost you the stipend, grades and academic standing, not just the degree.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register in TIGP's online portal during the November-February window, upload electronic files and have referees submit recommendations online; if you pass the preliminary evaluation, post original transcripts and test reports to the TIGP Office in Taipei before the deadline.
